Hosted work\\nuses the selected tool index or `docs/notes/harnessctl-reference.md#concise-hosted-authoring`.\\nDo not combine their arguments. A creation request supplies no missing fact. |\\n| Proposed method, check, evidence destination | Choose within the requested design scope; label it planned. |\\n\\nFor an intent, ask which change in the user's situation is needed and how the\\nowner will know it helped, when those inputs are missing. An audience name or\\nreplacement output alone does not answer those questions. Code or one same-type record cannot establish their\\nabsence. Use the current\\nevaluator result; do not reconstruct lifecycle rules or load all later stages.\\nWhen a supplied helper restricts commands, its tool index gives the export\\nspelling; the direct-client example above does not add permission or helper flags.\\n\\nFor each report claim, inspect its exact request/result or exported manifest.\\nUse the actual operation and outcome fields, not a filename, earlier summary or\\nremembered sequence. Orientation grants no\\nimplementation, decision, Git, credential or external-action right.\\n\"}, {\"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\README.md\", \"sha256\": \"fbf52d7ea22bab1dc9e4441ed14900dac8707faee648c6291addc45d3186984e\", \"bytes\": 15576, \"text\": \"# Hosted artifact sandbox\\n\\nOne Python service provides HTTP commands and shared HTTP/MCP reads over one\\nMemgraph database. Git remains the repository's formal authority. The sandbox\\nimports a fixed snapshot and prepares drafts. The explicit Phase 3 test-copy mode\\ncan rehearse lifecycle actions on new test records. It cannot replace imported\\ndecisions or authorize real work or publication. RISK-HAG-001 remains raised:\\napplication query controls do not prove database-enforced read-only access.\\n\\nPhase 2 was verified in VREC-HAG-004. The private lifecycle pilot under WO-HAG-008\\nwas verified in [VREC-HAG-005](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification-records/VREC-HAG-005.md)\\nand integrated through PR #542. Its eight VER-HAG-006 scenarios passed.\\nThe separate native Codex/Claude qualification under WO-HAG-009 is\\n[in progress](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-009/report.md).\\nNo public service, release, authority cutover or production claim is supplied here.\\n\\n## Inputs\\n\\nUse a Linux/amd64 Docker engine with Compose and Python 3.11+ on the operator\\nhost. The service uses the immutable CPython 3.13.16 image in [Dockerfile](Dockerfile),\\nMemgraph 3.13.1 in [compose.yaml](compose.yaml), hashed [Python dependencies](requirements.lock)\\nand hashed [Git packages](system-packages.lock.json). Use only public test data.\\nKeep all outputs outside the checkout. Preserve volumes until restore comparison\\nand qualification finish. The API binds loopback; the database has no host port.\\n\\nThe governor is public evaluator 0.22.1, wheel SHA-256\\n`cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053`.\\nCandidate remote client 0.22.2 lives in another environment. Unpublished plugin\\n0.2.7 bundles the unchanged evaluator and matching remote guidance. Service\\n0.1.0.dev1 owns server dependencies; the core checker keeps zero runtime dependencies.\\n\\n## Build the exact combination\\n\\nCommit the reviewed implementation. Follow the existing\\n[release build sequence](../docs/notes/developing-se-harness.md#release-sequences)\\nto produce the 0.22.2 candidate wheel and its two-build replay JSON at that commit.\\nUse the public 0.22.1 wheel as `EVALUATOR_WHEEL`. Resolve uppercase placeholders\\nto absolute paths or selected values. Keep each path as one argument.\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py prepare --repository REPO --output PACKAGE_OUT --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --client-replay CLIENT_REPLAY_JSON --evaluator-wheel EVALUATOR_WHEEL --image LOCAL_IMAGE\\n```\\n\\nThe command refuses a dirty checkout or client replay from another commit. It\\nreads exact Git blobs, uses the existing development plugin assembler, builds\\nthe service image, and records actual component identities. Outputs are:\\n\\n- `combination.json`: built identities, marked qualification pending.\\n- `configuration/config.json`: non-secret selection for that combination.\\n- `credentials.json`: generated test principals; keep this file private.\\n- `plugin/`: separate Codex and Claude development archives and extracted trees.\\n- `candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`: the selected deployment recipe.\\n- Command results and image metadata, including failures.\\n\\nReadiness verifies the selected release, installed service bytes, runtime,\\ndatabase version/configuration, schema and complete tuple. It is not assurance.\\n\\n## Stage the historical source\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/stage.py REPO REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/reference-manifest.json SOURCE_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThis writes `source/`, `source-manifest.json` and `source-inventory.json` from\\nexact Git blobs, including original code/evidence bindings. It does not execute\\nsource files. Create a new Docker volume `SOURCE_VOLUME` and copy those three\\nentries into its root. On Windows, archive the entries and extract inside Docker\\nto avoid slow small-file reads through a Windows bind mount. Retain the archive\\ndigest and copy command. Compose mounts this source read-only.\\n\\n## Initialize and start\\n\\nSet these environment variables for every Compose command:\\n\\n| Name | Selected value |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE` | Built `LOCAL_IMAGE`; retain its inspected immutable identity |\\n| `HAG_HTTP_PORT` | An unused loopback port, for example `18080` |\\n| `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` | Populated `SOURCE_VOLUME` |\\n| `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/configuration` |\\n| `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | Absolute `PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json` |\\n\\nChoose a new Compose project `PROJECT_NAME`. `COMPOSE_FILE` is the generated\\n`candidate-source/server/compose.yaml`.\\n\\n```text\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d graph\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE run --rm service init\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE up -d service\\ndocker compose -p PROJECT_NAME -f COMPOSE_FILE exec -T service harness-hosted ready\\n```\\n\\nWait for database availability before initialization and service readiness before\\nclient operations. Initialization is explicit; ordinary startup does not migrate\\nor repair a schema. `/health` means alive; authenticated `/v1/status` means ready.\\n\\nInstall `CLIENT_WHEEL` with `pip --no-deps` into a separate disposable environment.\\nIts Python is `CLIENT_PYTHON`. Use `-I -m se_harness remote`, never that candidate\\nas the governor. Read the extracted plugin's setup **Hosted sandbox selection**,\\nthen harness-orient or change. Native host discovery must be tested separately\\nwhere required; extracting files does not prove a host loaded the plugin.\\n\\n## Test the actual packages\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_service.py --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest SOURCE_OUT/source-manifest.json --scenario-fixture REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:PORT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n```\\n\\nThe packaged client imports and retries, retrieves the fixed work context, creates\\nand revises a draft, refuses invalid/stale writes, recovers a receipt, compares\\nviews, reads Cypher, runs the released check and freezes the draft. Each request\\nand result is retained. Its report lists remaining checks; it is not full acceptance.\\n\\nRun `tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_boundaries.py` with installed service\\ndependencies in a separate Compose service process. Mount the test directory\\nread-only and a new output directory. Pass `--walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_OUT` and\\n`--output BOUNDARY_OUT`. Default checks cover protected/malformed requests,\\nconcurrent connections, transaction faults, HTTP/MCP parity and resource limits.\\nFault hooks exist only in the test process, never on a network route.\\n\\nUse `--only lost_reply` with a separately installed candidate `--client-python`\\nand `--client-wheel` inside that process for lost-response recovery. If earlier\\nchecks advanced the context, pass their final `--continuation` JSON. Inspect the\\nretained operation before retrying any interrupted write. Never invent a new\\nexpected version or operation key to make a failed test succeed.\\n\\nRun `qualify_history.py` through the isolated released evaluator with `-I`, the\\nmounted original `--source`, `--manifest`, fixed `--fixture`, new `--output`, and\\nwalkthrough `005-work-context-result.json` as `--hosted-result`. This independent\\nprojection compares the evaluator result and recomputes legacy path/code hashes.\\n\\nFollow the complete [VER-HAG-001 matrix](../docs/engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification/VER-HAG-001.md),\\nincluding import variants, missing bindings, tuple/schema failures, measured\\nlimits and native plugin observations. Skipped or absent cases are unperformed.\\nRun the applicable repository regression and distribution checks.\\n\\nRun `qualify_integrity.py` in a disposable service process with the same mounts,\\nwalkthrough and current continuation. Supply its separately installed candidate\\n`--client-python`. This checks altered deployment identities, installed service\\ncontracts, evaluator substitution, and broken context-base links. Its file edits\\naffect only the disposable container; its graph edits always roll back. Do not run\\nit inside the serving container. Passing these checks does not complete the other\\nscenario requirements.\\n\\nRun `qualify_imports.py` with the walkthrough, current continuation and a new\\noutput directory. It creates disposable copies of the original source to test\\nduplicate IDs and unresolved targets. It also rejects unsupported import formats\\nand changed bytes under the original provenance. These negative tests must not\\nchange the database.\\n\\n`qualify_time.py` measures the configured five-second database read-transaction\\nlimit. Its stress query is a direct driver test, outside the public read grammar.\\nIt must produce a resource-limit refusal. This does not by itself prove a slow\\nquery's HTTP response or replace the public Cypher admission checks.\\n\\n## Restart and restore\\n\\nKeep the same `HAG_*` environment and stop other test writers. Use a fresh output\\nand an unused restore port:\\n\\n```text\\npython REPO/server/scripts/qualify.py recover --compose COMPOSE_FILE --project PROJECT_NAME --output RECOVERY_OUT --restore-port RESTORE_PORT\\n```\\n\\nThe command fingerprints the acknowledged graph, restarts the original, stops\\nwriters/database for a consistent backup, resumes the original, and restores\\ninto a new `PROJECT_NAME-restore` volume. It refuses an existing restore volume.\\nIt compares both copies at the cutoff and records times, storage, archive digest\\nand commands. Keep the backup and both volumes. Record the archive's retained\\nlocation outside Git. This proves no power-loss, production RPO/RTO or migration claim.\\n\\n## Protocol and limits\\n\\nSee the [protocol guide](../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md) and closed\\n[command](contracts/remote-v1.json), [read](contracts/read-v1.json) and\\n[result](contracts/result-v1.json) schemas. Views are explicit. Domain and MCP\\nreads share one handler. Partial reads cannot support a governing-context claim.\\n\\nLimits: 2,500 imported artifacts; 10,000 retained revisions; 1 MiB per document;\\n64 MiB of formal import content; two evaluator slots; 500 aggregate read rows;\\n2 MiB per response; depth eight; five seconds per Cypher query; 120 seconds per\\nevaluator process. Preserve measured limitations and RISK-HAG-001. Do not expose\\nthe sandbox on a shared or untrusted network.\\n\\n## Phase 3: private lifecycle rehearsal\\n\\nThis is an opt-in test project. Supplied decision actors are synthetic labels.\\nGit remains authoritative for real definitions and decisions. Authentication and\\ndatabase ACL implementation are deferred; keep the existing private controls.\\n\\n1. Build the clean candidate client with the pinned recipe above. Prepare the\\n   service with the same command above, adding `--phase3`. The configuration selects\\n   schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`. These are local qualification packages;\\n   do not publish them or replace the user's installed plugin.\\n2. Create the small synthetic source fixture outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/prepare_lifecycle_fixture.py --evaluator-python RELEASED_PYTHON --output FIXTURE_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   `RELEASED_PYTHON` is the absolute Python path for public evaluator 0.22.1. This\\n   command uses `-I`, creates an ordinary disposable Git repository, validates the\\n   seed records and stages exact Git blobs. Copy `FIXTURE_OUT/staged/` into a new\\n   source volume with the volume procedure above.\\n3. Use a new Compose project and graph volume. Set `HAG_SERVICE_IMAGE`,\\n   `HAG_CONFIG_DIRECTORY`, `HAG_CREDENTIAL_FILE`, `HAG_SOURCE_VOLUME` and a free\\n   loopback `HAG_HTTP_PORT`. Start the stack and run its explicit `init`. Do not\\n   migrate or reuse a Phase 2 volume. Read authenticated status and require the\\n   expected package identities, schema revision 2 and `test_copy: true`.\\n4. Install `CLIENT_WHEEL` into a separate environment. Run the packaged-client\\n   walkthrough, keeping its output outside the checkout:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   python REPO/tests/hosted_artifact_graph/qualify_pilot.py --repository REPO --client-python CLIENT_PYTHON --client-wheel CLIENT_WHEEL --configuration PACKAGE_OUT/configuration/config.json --credentials PACKAGE_OUT/credentials.json --source-manifest FIXTURE_OUT/staged/source-manifest.json --endpoint ENDPOINT --output WALKTHROUGH_OUT\\n   ```\\n\\n   The runner authors new test definitions, exercises a failed gate and an invalid\\n   edge, accepts definitions, starts work, records a paired risk/decision, retains\\n   handoff evidence, and prepares and assesses a test VREC and RLS. One record may cover several work orders (WO) at the same commit.                                        |\\n| `release_contract`    | `REL-`    | Defines permitted release scope, gates, rollback conditions, and authority limits.                                                                                           | When a release record (RLS) is proposed.                                                                                                                 |\\n| `release_record`      | `RLS-`    | Records preparation and the later release decision for verified work at one exact commit.                                                                                    | When a formal release is proposed. Preparing the record does not release the work.                                                                       |\\n| `decision`            | `DEC-`    | Records a question, options, recommendation, decision maker, affected artifacts, and the eventual answer. It can also record a deviation from one specification (SPEC) rule. | A question blocks a transition, affects more than one artifact, or must remain recorded after approval; or work cannot meet a specification (SPEC) rule. |\\n| `risk`                | `RISK-`   | Records a threat, an owner, and a next action. Scoring and categories are optional.                                                                                          | A concern needs follow-up. A separate decision (DEC) is used when the concern must block work.                                                           |\\n| `operating_contract`  | `OPS-`    | Defines continuing service, support, monitoring, or operational assurance obligations.                                                                                       | Ongoing operational commitments apply. Omitting the record does not prove those commitments have been met.                                               |\\n\\nCode, tests, acceptance scenarios, evidence files, commits, dashboards, tickets,\\nand conversations are not additional formal artifact types. They may support\\nor be referenced by formal artifacts but do not grant authority by themselves.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"47268c9ec1e3551fb547ad3d1ef7b8da0b773b52b3a4364f42c36cc64f98bf83\"}, {\"heading\": \"artifact-locations\", \"title\": \"Artifact locations\", \"anchor\": \"artifact-locations\", \"start_line\": 63, \"end_line\": 96, \"content\": \"## Artifact locations\\n\\nNew formal artifacts use these directories below\\n`docs/engineering/DOMAIN/`. `DOMAIN` is the selected domain name. These paths\\ndescribe storage, not authority; the artifact ID, metadata, and typed links\\nremain authoritative. Use the supported authoring command to obtain the actual\\npath. Do not move existing records merely to match this table.\\n\\n| Artifact | TYPE | Directory |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Intent (INT) | `intent` | `intent/` |\\n| Capability (CAP) | `capability` | `capabilities/` |\\n| Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | `requirements/` |\\n| Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | `specifications/` |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) | `architecture` | `architecture/` |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) | `adr` | `architecture/adr/` |\\n| Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | `verification/` |\\n| Work order (WO) | `work_order` | `work-orders/` |\\n| Verification record (VREC) | `verification_record` | `verification-records/` |\\n| Release contract (REL) | `release_contract` | `release/` |\\n| Release record (RLS) | `release_record` | `releases/` |\\n| Operating contract (OPS) | `operating_contract` | `operations/` |\\n| Decision (DEC) | `decision` | `decisions/` |\\n| Risk (RISK) | `risk` | `risks/` |\\n\\nThe same domain has `evidence/` for retained work-order evidence and\\n`acceptance/` for acceptance scenarios. These are supporting files, not new\\nformal artifact types. Legacy flat artifact locations remain readable and\\nMUST NOT be moved by an upgrade without separate authority.\\n\\nTemplates under `docs/engineering/templates/` are authoring assets. They are\\nexcluded from active-artifact validation and grant no authority. Use\\n`capture-verification` and `prepare-release` for commit-bound VREC and RLS\\ninstances; an edited template is not a substitute for their derived evidence.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8df276d2f837c4dcc663dbdb42c67cbb6f8fe3bf4abcb53acf86bc7538269a72\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DEFINITION_LINKS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"75b0c06f90fbb219fc31684a1a2d97987215dbada20e335656e45a57532c3010\", \"bytes\": 3505, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"title\": \"Links between definitions\", \"anchor\": \"links-between-definitions\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 35, \"content\": \"## Links between definitions\\n\\nAn arrow points from the artifact that records the link to the artifact it\\nreferences. These links describe meaning and coverage, not execution order.\\n\\nRepository validation, draft validation and work-order preflight share the\\ndeclared source/relation/target types. A supplied undeclared relation or a target\\nof the wrong type is invalid even when no work order selects the artifact.\\nPreflight still evaluates readiness only for its selected governing chain.\\nThe read-only draft query permits specific unfinished authoring slots; ordinary\\nvalidation and approval retain their completeness requirements.\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CAP[\\\"Capability (CAP)\\\"] -->|derives_from| INT[\\\"Intent (INT)\\\"]\\n    REQ[\\\"Requirement (REQ)\\\"] -->|derives_from| CAP\\n    SPEC[\\\"Specification (SPEC)\\\"] -->|specifies| REQ\\n    VER[\\\"Verification contract (VER)\\\"] -->|verifies| REQ\\n    ARCH[\\\"Architecture (ARCH)\\\"] -->|addresses| REQ\\n    ARCH -->|conforms_to| SPEC\\n    ADR[\\\"Architecture decision (ADR)\\\"] -->|decides| ARCH\\n```\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Capability (CAP) \\u2192 Intent (INT) | `derives_from` | Each active capability (CAP) names one or more active intents (INT). |\\n| Requirement (REQ) \\u2192 Capability (CAP) | `derives_from` | Each active requirement (REQ) names one or more active capabilities (CAP). |\\n| Specification (SPEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `specifies` | Each requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO) needs one or more selected active specifications (SPEC). |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `addresses` | The architecture (ARCH) names every requirement (REQ) that materially drives its structure. |\\n| Architecture (ARCH) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `conforms_to` | For each addressed requirement (REQ), the selected architecture (ARCH) names at least one selected specification (SPEC) covering it. |\\n| Architecture decision (ADR) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) | `decides` | Each selected architecture (ARCH) that requires a design decision has at least one selected active architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Verification contract (VER) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `verifies` | Each selected requirement (REQ) has one or more selected active verification contracts (VER). |\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7e7361437700c3a1bf7d9add02accf3a4d3ee3fa48dbdc0ba0b991b40514071a\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}, {\"heading\": \"intent\", \"title\": \"intent\", \"anchor\": \"intent\", \"start_line\": 76, \"end_line\": 84, \"content\": \"## intent\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain the present problem, who it affects, and the outcome wanted.\\n- What is the smallest useful outcome, and which needs and constraints are actually agreed?\\n- Say how the owner will know the change helped; an honest baseline may be `not measured`.\\n- State the important scope limits. Create a new intent when the desired outcome changes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"291e8274f0c400a3d2d1ecdd56f2c10d68ab6cb40f667076a034e44d87c05e42\"}, {\"heading\": \"capability\", \"title\": \"capability\", \"anchor\": \"capability\", \"start_line\": 85, \"end_line\": 93, \"content\": \"## capability\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Say what an actor should be able to do and any relevant conditions.\\n- Does each supported case serve an agreed need under those conditions?\\n- Link the intent it serves. The graph lists the derived requirements.\\n- Put implementation details where they help the implementer; no required `can ... under` wording.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee6452eeeb618cbe10c941638e7f6be38d2709f53e169920c2d3d012c94ce978\"}, {\"heading\": \"requirement\", \"title\": \"requirement\", \"anchor\": \"requirement\", \"start_line\": 59, \"end_line\": 75, \"content\": \"## requirement\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- State the observable behavior and why it is needed. Ordinary language is accepted; `SHALL` is optional.\\n- What agreed outcome does this obligation serve, for whom and under which conditions? Separate requirements from assumptions and speculative needs.\\n- Include a concrete acceptance condition in `Examples`, `Acceptance`, `measure`, `verification_notes`, or a linked verification contract.\\n- Name the source capability and a verification method. Supported method arrays contain `test`, `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration`; retained text methods remain readable.\\n- Replace unfinished placeholders and resolve blocking decisions before approval.\\n\\n### Guidance\\n\\nWrite enough for someone to implement and check the behavior. Use the template's\\nsections when helpful. Word counts, sentence shapes and numbers of code references\\nare not checked. Writing hints never block approval. Optional metadata must still\\nhave a valid value when supplied.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"333872b200842af881c6c22cfcb0631897071421f423885b2702ac6b72c75770\"}, {\"heading\": \"specification\", \"title\": \"specification\", \"anchor\": \"specification\", \"start_line\": 94, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"## specification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Explain what an implementation must do, including meaningful failure behavior.\\n- Is each promised behavior necessary? Could a simpler contract meet the agreed need? Prescribe a mechanism only when it is a necessary constraint.\\n- Link the requirements and show an example someone can check.\\n- Give a rule a stable identifier when evidence or a decision needs to refer to it.\\n- Check that supplied rule references exist and identifiers are unambiguous.\\n\\nMissing summaries and ambiguous rule references may produce draft hints. Hints\\nhelp a reviewer; they do not withhold approval. Existing approved text need not\\nbe rewritten to adopt these checklists.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"7aeefa5f4ed363ecdef5185d2b776c6fdd9146ece8e2bfd7ae1ee852f0acf6e1\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"
}

Inspect the preview before creation; replace\\n`VER-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --id VER-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nNo harness command writes the verification method or pass criteria. The execution\\nand verification processes later perform the checks and assess the evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"16a9ea7323450e244b26edd2d1ad757048124b627bcfffa157c8b173f57f363c\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release or operating contract\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"start_line\": 166, \"end_line\": 220, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release or operating contract\\n\\n**Inputs:** A proposed release or ongoing operating obligation, its scope,\\nexisting work-order or requirement IDs, and any accepted contract that may\\nalready cover it.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** A completed release-contract (REL) or operating-contract\\n  (OPS) draft when needed. An accepted contract is reused only if its meaning\\n  and scope already cover the proposed obligation.\\n- **Transient working material:** Selection notes, new IDs and paths, and\\n  unresolved questions. No release or operating authorization is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Decide which obligation applies: release scope uses `release_contract`;\\n   continuing assurance uses `operating_contract`. Do not create both by default.\\n2. Read existing contracts selected for reuse. If an accepted contract needs\\n   changed meaning, use the accepted-definition amendment boundary; do not edit\\n   it through this draft-creation procedure.\\n3. For a missing contract, use the supported domain and artifact creation\\n   sequence from \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Inspect the dry-run result and use its\\n   returned `allocated_id` in the creation command.\\n4. Complete the generated body and accountable metadata. For a REL, record\\n   release scope, version conditions, rollback, and evidence expectations.\\n   For an OPS, record measurable observability, support, and operating obligations.\\n5. Set `REL.gates` to every existing work-order ID covered by the release\\n   contract, or `OPS.assures` to every existing requirement ID for which it\\n   claims continuing assurance. Do not leave invented or unresolved IDs.\\n6. Apply `## release_contract` or `## operating_contract` and its `### Checklist`\\n   in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. Validate the completed draft and resolve findings within the proposed scope.\\n8. Include the contract in [Authorize the work](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure) for the exact human decision.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nHere `TYPE` is `release_contract` or `operating_contract`, selected in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id CONTRACT-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The applicable contract is covered by an unchanged accepted\\nrecord or a completed draft ready for its decision. Unresolved amendments\\nremain visible and block dependent work.\\n\\n**Later use:** An accepted REL governs release preparation. An accepted OPS\\ngoverns its stated continuing obligations after delivery. Perform the checks\\nand follow-up actions named in the OPS at its specified triggers; one successful\\ndelivery does not establish continuing conformance. External operating actions\\nstill require their exact authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"723a469b890666ae4b1e7b95a6231200a6794e6b792fef8e043ed82bc4f96ce5\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"verification\", \"title\": \"verification\", \"anchor\": \"verification\", \"start_line\": 126, \"end_line\": 135, \"content\": \"## verification\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Independence: expected values derive from the requirements and specifications, never from candidate output.\\n- A requirement-to-evidence matrix with a pass condition per requirement.\\n- Cover normal behavior and meaningful failure outcomes or risks; do not invent failure scenarios to fill a template.\\n- What accepted behavior or quality does each test or CI check establish? Cover distinct relevant outcomes, reuse applicable evidence, and avoid mirroring every implementation branch or combination.\\n- Pass criteria name the platforms and the evaluator.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e6d36e5fe7a23845861e67079317f856b4f892d7f17c4f3d4dbdb4476edb7720\"}, {\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}, {\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"c4ffde0efff3a57df41cf6b282896e6827ea289607f8b73faa8f7c09d0c70213\", \"bytes\": 8654, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nRead [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo), [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope) and [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#work_order).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d2a9a7707114a465ebde20884e2a996807663ab4aa94ff11008f2360617efe50\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"title\": \"Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 143, \"content\": \"### Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, artifact inventory, definition drafts,\\namendment proposals, verification contracts (VER), risks (RISK), and\\nunresolved decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or completed work orders (WO) in `draft`.\\n  Applicable risks (RISK) and open decisions (DEC) updated with the actual\\n  work order (WO) links. Lifecycle states and dispositions are preserved.\\n  Approved work orders (WO) remain unchanged; proposed scope changes require\\n  review.\\n- **Transient working material:** The review handoff and evaluator results.\\n  Retain these under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Inspect the implementation and follow its callers, references and consumers.\\n   Check tests and fixtures, instructions and documentation, packaging and CI,\\n   and verification outputs where they apply. Keep the working inventory in\\n   the conversation or temporary storage outside the repository.\\n   Group each complete, independently verifiable outcome into one bounded\\n   work order with its necessary supporting changes.\\n2. Select an existing work order (WO) in `draft` for a unit only if its scope\\n   matches. Otherwise, create a new work order (WO) with the commands below.\\n3. Complete each draft using the field table below. In Expected change\\n   surface, name the inspected paths and give a short reason for each.\\n   Explain non-applicable areas and unknown destinations briefly.\\n4. Check that every selected requirement (REQ) has the specification (SPEC)\\n   and verification contract (VER) coverage defined in [Complete work scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope).\\n5. Apply `## work_order` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n6. Add the new work order (WO) IDs to applicable `threatens` relations in risks\\n   (RISK) and `concerns` or `blocks` relations in open decisions (DEC). Keep\\n   every blocked ID in `concerns`. Preserve any required pairing between the\\n   risk (RISK) and decision (DEC).\\n7. If the planned change needs a missing release or operating contract,\\n   use [Prepare a release or operating contract](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract) now that the work\\n   order IDs exist. Include its draft in the proposed package.\\n8. Run the validation command below.\\n9. Correct findings within the proposed drafts. Rerun validation after edits.\\n   Report unrelated findings separately. Retain findings that need a decision\\n   or an accepted-definition amendment as unresolved dependencies.\\n10. Run the selected-work check below for each proposed work order (WO).\\n    Supply every planned file from Expected change surface with\\n    `--planned-path`. Inspect `scope.preparation`: resolve uncovered or\\n    invalid paths in the draft before requesting approval. A successful\\n    command exit does not establish coverage or a complete impact analysis.\\n    Explain future generated destinations using\\n    [Generated outputs](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs).\\n11. Present the outcome, scope, artifact IDs and paths, validation results,\\n    unresolved decisions (DEC), and unapplied amendments. Include the\\n    evaluator's reported next action for each selected work order (WO).\\n\\n| Field or section | Content |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `Objective` | The outcome this work order (WO) will deliver. |\\n| `In scope` / `Out of scope` | The boundaries from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) assigned to this work order (WO). |\\n| `Constraints` | The conditions from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) that apply to this work. |\\n| `Expected change surface` | Inspected planned paths, the reason for each, and unresolved destinations. |\\n| `[execution_scope].paths` | Exact repository-relative files or component directories ending in `/`. Use forward slashes; no wildcards, absolute paths, or `..`. |\\n| `Authorized decision envelope` | What the implementer may decide and what requires another accountable decision. |\\n| `Required verification` / `Evidence to record` | The checks and retained outputs defined in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified). |\\n| `Stop and escalate conditions` | The conditions that require pausing this work. |\\n| `Completion report format` | The required report of completed behavior, checks, limitations, and next accountable decision. |\\n| `[assurance]` | `commit_bound_verification`, its `rationale`, and `decided_by`. Apply the classification rules in [Assurance classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Record the human who confirmed the classification; an agent may propose it and record that human's decision. |\\n| `[relations]` | `implements` \\u2192 requirements (REQ); `specifications` \\u2192 specifications (SPEC); `verification` \\u2192 verification contracts (VER); `architecture` \\u2192 applicable architectures (ARCH) and required architecture decisions (ADR). |\\n\\nFor PR-based work, include the proposed [review-publication grant](AUTHORITY.md#review-publication-authority)\\nin the decision envelope. Name its repository, source branch, target branch\\nand selected work. Include both the ready-record publication and the later\\ndecision-only push in the expected scope. Present that grant explicitly with\\nimplementation approval; do not infer it from ordinary work authority.\\n\\nIf the assurance classification has not been confirmed, present it as a\\nproposal in the review handoff. Report the missing decision. Do not fill\\n`decided_by` with the draft author's name or an example identity to satisfy\\nvalidation. The human may confirm the classification while reviewing the\\nwork order; record that decision before previewing approval.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new work order (WO), run the creation sequence from [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions).\\nInspect the preview before creation; replace `WO-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --id WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nValidate the formal artifacts after completing the drafts and links:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nInspect each proposed work order (WO) using its actual ID:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nTo assess the proposed file list, repeat `--planned-path` for every file:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --planned-path PATH --planned-path ANOTHER-PATH --json\\n```\\n\\nThis option is available only when the selected released evaluator supports\\nit. If it is unavailable, report that version gap; do not run candidate\\nsource to govern the repository.\\n\\nThe optional planning view evaluates no checkpoint. It reports explicit\\nscope matches, existing automatic admission, uncovered paths and invalid\\ndeclarations. It does not inspect dependencies for the agent, prove that\\nthe supplied list is complete, or turn planned paths into observed changes.\\nDo not combine it with checkpoint or actual-change inputs.\\n\\nValidation does not approve the change. The checkpoint-free `check` reports\\nlifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint gates.\\n\\n**Completion:** Draft work orders (WO) are presented for review with their\\ngoverning artifacts and evaluator results. Every unresolved dependency is\\nidentified. Preparation does not approve or start execution.\\n\\n**Later use:** The authorization process reviews this artifact package,\\nresolves approval blockers, and applies permitted lifecycle transitions.\\nOnly the formal artifacts carry lasting definitions and work authority;\\ntransient working material is not persisted in the repository.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ee93a263dcebc650ee59519ecaafa4c005120db60b83b8acc6bf4191efe3c8dd\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "command": "\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\.cache\\\\codex-runtimes\\\\codex-primary-runtime\\\\dependencies\\\\native\\\\powershell\\\\pwsh.exe\" -Command 'C:/Users/mathi/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe -I C:/Users/mathi/Documents/Codex/2026-09-20/verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se/work/hag-functional29-20261011/codex-241/native/inputs/native_call.py instructions --section \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#links-from-work-orders-wo\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs\"'",
  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"title\": \"Links from work orders (WO)\", \"anchor\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 28, \"content\": \"## Links from work orders (WO)\\n\\nA work order (WO) selects the definitions and verification contracts (VER) that govern\\nits execution. Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. \"sha256\": \"4e1707f6664157a9ab47e8b38301090551b35153b91bd10315a41ee39aae2984\", \"bytes\": 5575, \"text\": \"# Private lifecycle rehearsal wire contract\\n\\nThe v2 endpoint accepts only `lifecycle-v2.json`. Every request and result selects\\ntest data. Git remains authoritative for real work. Existing v1 routes and the\\nseven read-only MCP tools keep their contract; they cannot dispatch v2 actions.\\nIn an explicitly configured test project their results use\\n`se-harness-graph-read/v2`, with a required test-copy label. Ordinary Phase 2\\nprojects retain their v1 read result shapes. Revision byte hashing is unchanged;\\ntest revisions add explicit test-copy provenance, without rewriting v1 fixtures.\\n\\n`inspect` accepts check, preflight and validate. `preview` runs a mutation in a\\ndiscarded projection and returns its input digest and complete proposed file\\neffects. `apply` requires that digest, reruns the released checks, and commits\\nthe complete result once. A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}]}\r\n",

Review the governing definitions against the relevant checklists in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n5. Check that the proposed work has defined scope, verification coverage,\\n   assurance classification, and accountable humans for the required decisions.\\n6. List the blockers affecting the selected package. Definition artifacts cannot be selected\\nwith `check`; their transition gates are evaluated by the previews in [Apply the selected transitions](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#apply-the-selected-transitions).\\n\\nBefore proposing a definition for approval, resolve its template placeholders.\\nIf it contains an `Open decisions` section, confirm that no unresolved decision\\nremains before setting that section to `None`. A decision right describes which\\naction that person or agent is authorized to perform. Being a Human does not\\ngrant every right in this table. Being an Agent grants none by itself.\\n\\nUse the artifact's recorded ownership and any existing explicit delegation to\\nidentify the accountable human. Resolve a team name or ownership label to the\\nhuman making this decision. A proposed `owners` value, an example actor name,\\nor authorship of a draft MUST NOT assign decision authority.\\n\\nApproval, verification acceptance, and release decisions MUST be made by an\\nauthorized human. An agent MAY prepare the material and apply that human's\\nrecorded decision when authorized to do so. Applying the decision does not\\nmake the agent its author. |\\n|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|\\n| order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           |                                               | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent under the approval of every selected work order.                                                                    | Exact candidate, selected work and verification contracts, retained evidence, and passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept verification for the selected candidate.                                                                | Ready record, assessed evidence, and the exact verify, reject, or supersede decision.                             | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration or release-preparation path.                                                           | Exact candidate, destination, and coverage required by that path.                                                 | One path-specific instruction.                                                                       |\\n| `DR-RLS-PREPARE`           | Human authorizes the release inputs; a Human or Agent may carry out the preparation.                                               | Exact release contract, candidate, included work, verification coverage, version, and passing preparation checks. | One `ready` release record; no release decision.                                                     |\\n| `DR-RLS-DECIDE`            | Human authorized to make the release decision.                                                                                     | Ready release record, assessed contract obligations, and the exact release or reject decision.                    | Decision on that release record only.                                                                |\\n| `DR-EXTERNAL-ACTION`       | Human authorized for the exact external action. A Human or Agent may execute the authorized operation.                             | Action, immutable target, destination, prerequisites, and recovery conditions.                                    | Authorization limited to that operation; the subsequent tool result records its actual effects.      |\\n| `DR-RELATED-RECORD-SELECT` | Human or Agent; no decision authority is needed for inspection.                                                                    | Exact existing artifact ID.                                                                                       | Read-only selection.                                                                                 |\\n| `DR-REMEDIATION-SCOPE`     | Human authorized to change the affected definition or work scope.                                                                  | Failed criterion and proposed bounded correction.                                                                 | Explicit authority for the revised scope.                                                            |\\n| `DR-DECISION-DISPOSE`      | Human accountable for the artifact blocked by the decision; for a deviation, the human accountable for the affected specification. | Open or deferred decision, selected option or disposition, exact reason, and any required revisit trigger.        | Recorded disposition and any declared paired-risk effect. Other blocked artifacts keep their states. |\\n\\nFor a lifecycle decision, the `--decision` value identifies its actual\\ndecision-maker. When an agent applies a human decision, that value is the\\nhuman who made it. For start and completion under approved execution, it is\\nthe actual Human or Agent executor. Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. Preparation `--owner` values identify the preparation actor, not\\na future assurance or release decision-maker.\\n\\nFor `decide`, when an owner label differs from the actual human's identity,\\nuse `--authority-owner OWNER` only after establishing that human's authority\\nfor the exact decision. Keep `--decision ACTOR` as the actual human. The\\nevaluator checks that OWNER holds the existing decision right and records it\\nseparately as `authority_owner`. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. In particular, do not\\n   imply approval, a transition, verification, release, a Git action,\\n   publication, deployment, or operation that did not occur.\\n4. The final lifecycle state and the accountable human or agent. When a\\n   decision is required, name the exact decision and authority needed.\\n5. The command's argument values and boundaries, or the operative meaning of\\n   the suggested response.\\n\\nOnly complete alternatives declared by the workflow may be shown. No new decision or scope is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read the selected artifact's type and current state. Do not treat a prior\\n   conversation summary as current state.\\n2. For a work order, verification record, release record, or decision, obtain\\n   its current result with `check`.\\n3. For a definition, use its recorded state and the explicitly requested human\\n   decision. A permitted transition preview evaluates that decision. The\\n   selected release does not accept definition IDs in `check`.\\n4. For a risk, read its record and any paired decision. Use [Record risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change) for\\n   creation and [Resolve approval blockers](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers) for a requested decision disposition.\\n   Do not infer a work-order stop from an unpaired risk alone.\\n5. If a returned command is unsupported by the exact selected release, report\\n   that contract/version mismatch. Do not repair it by inventing another next\\n   action, changing record state, or running candidate source.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse only the supported types named in action 2. It does not delegate the decision itself. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. Before using its execution grant, read [AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval](AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval). For a scope finding, read [RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked](RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5581ca4e192b2a3847952cdb19582916ed96242a14941b1e5a8a610be996e1dd\"}, {\"heading\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"title\": \"Start the selected work\", \"anchor\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 104, \"content\": \"### Start the selected work\\n\\n**Inputs:** The approved work order (WO), actual executor identity, and\\ncurrent execution context.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `in_progress`\\n  with a lifecycle-history entry when start succeeds.\\n- **Transient working material:** Start-check and transition results.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If the work order (WO) is already `in_progress`, inspect the recorded start\\n   and resume unapplied work. Do not replay the start transition.\\n2. Otherwise, run start preflight under the existing approval.\\n3. Preview the transition to `in_progress` using the actual executor identity.\\n4. Apply the same transition only when preflight and the preview pass.\\n5. Inspect the resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected work order (WO) is `in_progress`, or its start\\nis blocked with an explicit reason. Existing approval covers a permitted\\nstart; no duplicate human start decision is required.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Implement the approved scope](EXECUTE_WORK.md#implement-the-approved-scope) performs the authorized implementation.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2275126fa8b418eccbaacb1972d0140709337470ba8d190b6566fd16854328d1\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"title\": \"Authority from work approval\", \"anchor\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"start_line\": 134, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## Authority from work approval\\n\\nWork-order approval authorizes execution of its approved scope: start,\\nimplementation, local edits and commits, required checks, evidence capture,\\ncompletion recording, and required verification-record preparation. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. An older approval without\\nsuch a grant needs an authorized amendment for the remaining execution.\\nCurrent metadata or an actor label MUST NOT manufacture that historical grant.\\nIf the installed release cannot record the required authorization, stop the\\nremaining execution and report the missing historical grant and the lack of\\na supported amendment operation. Do not insert invented grant fields or\\nrewrite the old approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"a0ce00fccb8c1c8833455c14fe3ec75eaf01c597f0a1f46a24f7962ab1958f8c\"}]}]}\r\n",
