  "command": "\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\.cache\\\\codex-runtimes\\\\codex-primary-runtime\\\\dependencies\\\\native\\\\powershell\\\\pwsh.exe\" -Command 'C:/Users/mathi/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe -I C:/Users/mathi/Documents/Codex/2026-09-20/verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se/work/hag-functional29-20261011/codex-241/native/inputs/native_call.py instructions --section \"docs/engineering/harness/EXECUTE_WORK.md#retain-the-implementation-evidence\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#before-this-action\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks\"'",
  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"f094e7bc796ba1002c3fb2848adaccce6c4887e3d92503911bcafa4504a644fe\", \"bytes\": 11979, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"title\": \"Retain the implementation evidence\", \"anchor\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"start_line\": 155, \"end_line\": 210, \"content\": \"### Retain the implementation evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The implemented changes, verification contracts (VER), required\\nrepository checks, and work-order evidence locations.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** Actual check results, review findings, their\\n  resolution, and Git-derived handoff evidence at authorized evidence paths.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Evidence references may be added where the work order\\n  (WO) requires them. No lifecycle state changes here.\\n- **Transient working material:** A summary of remaining evidence gaps.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run every required check using its specified inputs and environment.\\n2. Retain the command arguments, working directory, runtime identity, exit\\n   status, output, and relevant file paths or digests.\\n3. Preserve failed results alongside later corrections and successful reruns.\\n4. Retain the material diff-review findings and their resolution.\\n5. Confirm that all required evidence files exist at the locations named by\\n   the work order (WO) or verification contract (VER).\\n6. Run review preflight.\\n7. Run the Git-derived handoff check with the trusted `BASE` from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n8. Inspect its written evidence and reported findings. Correct in-scope gaps\\n   and rerun affected checks.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase review --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nFor ordinary files listed in the work order\\u2019s `evidence_paths`, confirm that\\neach file exists inside the repository and contains the required evidence.\\nThese files do not need a machine header. Use the supported evidence command\\nfor generated packets; do not edit their evaluator-owned binding fields.\\n\\nThe Git-derived handoff command writes retained evidence. Confirm its output\\npaths are covered by the approved preparation scope. If the evaluator calls\\nfor creating or rebinding the handoff evidence packet, use:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl evidence REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --json\\n```\\n\\nThis command also writes a file. It does not run tests or make an unsupported\\nclaim true. Rerun the required handoff check after correcting the evidence gap.\\n\\n**Completion:** Required implementation checks pass and the actual evidence\\nis retained, or the exact missing or failed checks remain visible.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record implementation completion](EXECUTE_WORK.md#record-implementation-completion) requires passing handoff results. Verification later\\nassesses these retained files; they are not disposable planning notes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"4cccfe03ac5fe219da997051bb91053576f18e67e834f0036f93e9856e8f12a2\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore writing, read [Links for decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks), [Blocking decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions) and [Raised risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"title\": \"Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\", \"anchor\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"### Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, selected definitions, verification coverage,\\nand existing risks (RISK) found in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New risks (RISK) in `raised` for threats not already\\n  covered. A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`.   "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"risk\", \"title\": \"risk\", \"anchor\": \"risk\", \"start_line\": 188, \"end_line\": 198, \"content\": \"## risk\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\\n- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\\n- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1\\u20135); the command computes their product.\\n- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\\n- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\\n\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8815c9ff38ca34594404ab95cb0545053e209804030f3d635a50641d33559de9\"}, {\"heading\": \"decision\", \"title\": \"decision\", \"anchor\": \"decision\", \"start_line\": 171, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## decision\\n\\nA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\\nof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\\napproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\\nand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\\n- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\\n- A deviation also names `against = \\\"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\\\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\\n- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\\n- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\\n- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\\n- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}]}\r\n",

Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead7ade46e1090c644d789a5ca1155415aa2497561938b885e8316cd13aeb920\"}]}]}\r\n",

}

Confirm that the work and required evidence are complete.\\n2. Preview the completion transition using the executor's own identity.\\n3. Apply the same transition when the preview passes.\\n4. Inspect the resulting work order (WO).\\n5. Report the completed behavior, checks, limitations, and evaluator's next\\n   action. Preserve failures if completion was refused.\\n\\nUse the passing handoff result from the preceding step. A passing completion\\npreview does not replace the handoff check. If the implementation, governing\\nartifacts, or required evidence changed after handoff, rerun the affected\\nchecks before applying completion. If `harnessctl` refuses the retained\\nhandoff evidence, follow its reported corrective step.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The work order (WO) is `implemented`, or its completion is\\nblocked. Completion does not verify, release, or deliver the result.\\n\\n**Later use:** Work requiring commit-bound verification proceeds to\\n[Verify the outcome](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#establish-the-verification-scope).\\nAfter preparation, PR-based work first follows [Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package).\\nThen use the [verification request](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision)\\nwhen the ready record is eligible and its PR is confirmed. Local-only work\\nuses that verification request without a PR. The completion report introduces no\\nadditional human approval. An implemented work order (WO) classified `not_required`\\nneeds no new verification record (VREC); follow its actual next action and\\nany separately authorized delivery instruction.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e9c897ed3281727176649c1a128308da088e0f04282645d2c43a4c7a9a795649\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"84686ea50e0e220aadc024145b88e05d83a0eab01be361ab50e12716a8cf950a\", \"bytes\": 18538, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor preparation, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage). For a decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). For supersession only, also read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage). Read the exact candidate and retained evidence required by the selected contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"509b10e8e12887c623b12e5997e2baf7bcb193b87a24b63fe19795676bddc8a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"title\": \"Assess the verification evidence\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"### Assess the verification evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected candidate, accepted definitions, verification\\ncontracts (VER), and retained implementation evidence.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** A requirement-by-requirement assessment with\\n  actual check results and unresolved gaps at the specified evidence locations.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No verification decision or lifecycle transition.\\n- **Transient working material:** Review notes not required as retained evidence.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare the verification record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"start_line\": 108, \"end_line\": 169, \"content\": \"### Prepare the verification record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact candidate, selected work orders (WO), their verification\\ncontracts (VER), retained evidence, and existing preparation authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** One new verification record (VREC) in `ready` when\\n  capture is required and succeeds. Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}]}]}\r\n",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "status": "completed"

Local-only work does not acquire a PR requirement.\\n\\n**Inputs:** The ready verification record (VREC), candidate commit, evidence\\ndigests, assessment results, and accountable human's verification authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by the discussion or read-only gate check.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's exact verification, rejection,\\n  or supersession decision and reason where required.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Prepare the concise verification request below for the exact record,\\n   candidate, evidence, and unresolved findings.\\n2. For verification or rejection, evaluate the proposed target with the\\n   command below. Obtain the accountable human's decision on that exact verification record\\n   (VREC). Preserve the required independence from implementation.\\n4. Reuse a previous decision only while its record, candidate, evidence digests,\\n   authority, and current gates still match.\\n5. For rejection, retain the reason. For supersession, identify the exact\\n   eligible successor verification record (VREC).\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `verified` or `rejected` for `TARGET`. The evaluator determines whether\\nthat edge is legal. Supersession needs the successor input accepted by\\n`transition --reason`, which this check command does not accept.\\nA passed check is not the human decision.\\n\\n**Verification request:**\\n\\n- **Verification requested - [outcome]:** Name the useful result being assessed.\\n- **Delivered:** Describe the behavior delivered against the agreed outcome.\\n- **Evidence:** Summarize the requirement results and meaningful checks. Link\\n  the requirement-by-requirement assessment and retained evidence. Test counts\\n  support the explanation; they do not replace it.\\n- **Limits:** State material failures, skipped or unavailable checks, unassessed\\n  criteria, and residual uncertainty. Say that no material gaps are known only\\n  when the evidence supports it.\\n- **Your decision:** Explain that \\\"Verify result\\\" accepts this exact candidate\\n  against the agreed requirements. Merge and release remain separate decisions.\\n- **Review details:** For PR-based work, show the confirmed PR URL prominently.\\n  Identify the exact VREC and full candidate commit. Link its governing work\\n  orders, verification contracts, assessment, and evidence at the remote review\\n  commit so the owner can read them without access to the workstation.\\n  Local-only work uses its available review locations.\\n\\nLead with ordinary language and keep the request proportionate to the work.\\nDetails may be linked, but material gaps and the decision's scope must be\\nvisible in the request. Keep passed, failed, and not-assessed results distinct.\\nAn accepted risk needs its recorded decision reference; otherwise it remains\\nunresolved. No implementation actor infers acceptance from their own passing tests.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision) records only the selected decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"cdf0222448290088f6b56d69941badd6bd3bf0bf60c19e05ddba06b00033f081\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Historical candidate and evidence facts are preserved.\\n- **Transient working material:** The observed decision result and next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Recheck that the selected inputs still match the human decision.\\n2. Preview the exact transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Preserve\\nthe old record; do not rewrite its candidate or evidence to match a new result.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected verification record (VREC) has the recorded\\ndecision. Referenced work orders (WO) and release records (RLS) remain unchanged.\\n\\n**Later use:** For PR-based work, [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision)\\nas the final commit under the existing grant. Eligible verified coverage\\nsupports the selected delivery path.\\nA rejection or supersession follows the evaluator's remediation or selection\\nprocedure; it does not authorize new implementation scope.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"99e090908551d2012bdadac654496a2c14eefe9399b04112fcf067f6386854d7\"}]}]}\r\n",

Resolve an ambiguous destination with the requester.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a work order (WO), verification record (VREC), or release record (RLS)\\nas `ARTIFACT-ID`. Selection changes no lifecycle state.\\n\\n**Completion:** One delivery action and target are explicit. Selecting a path\\ndoes not authorize or perform its external action.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the delivery package](DELIVER_RESULT.md#prepare-the-delivery-package), [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required), [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required), [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action), [Perform the authorized delivery](DELIVER_RESULT.md#perform-the-authorized-delivery), [Confirm the delivery result](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-the-delivery-result) prepare, authorize, perform, and confirm that action.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3c62d9982634dc649143dfbaa6d84299d868a5b1f9f4d18861c99d673da2f01d\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RELEASE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-functional29-20261011\\\\codex-241\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RELEASE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"ce700f8f764c4425978f070d978d48eacafb927601f45e298c765f46dae90f7f\", \"bytes\": 7849, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore preparing, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage) and the selected REL/VREC records. Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 71, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected path, existing preparation authority, exact candidate,\\nand the release contract (REL) and eligible verified coverage required by that\\npath. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}]}]}\r\n",

Retain the actual human, decision reference and reviewed plan digest.\\n   Do not rewrite the plan when public observations arrive; retain them separately.\\n4. Retain a rejection reason when applicable.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `released` or `rejected` for `TARGET`, according to the proposed decision.\\nThe evaluator determines legality. A passed check does not supply approval.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is explicit, or remains pending.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#record-the-release-decision-when-required) records that decision. Execute listed delivery actions\\nunder the same complete-release authorization when their conditions still match.\\nOtherwise obtain only the exact external authority that is missing.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"3f8f1bc33363c8583a4b28560220ccaa7497990299624c53d90e1b364fecca78\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}]}]}\r\n",

The private\\nservice and candidate remote client are implemented under WO-HAG-001. Development\\nqualification is retained in VREC-HAG-004. Git remains authoritative. The pilot uses separately versioned\\n[closed operations](../../server/contracts/lifecycle-v2.md), exact multi-file\\nsnapshots and ordinary disposable Git history. Its eight required VER-HAG-006\\nscenarios passed, and mmzen verified\\n[VREC-HAG-005](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification-records/VREC-HAG-005.md).\\nPR #542 integrated that result. The existing\\nprivate access controls and RISK-HAG-001 remain in place.\\n\\n## Project and source identities\\n\\nThe explicit operator initialization command allocates a UUIDv4 `project_id`\\nonce and stores it on Project with `command_version = 0` and `schema_revision = 1`.\\nAn operator may supply a fixed UUID for a reproducible disposable test. Repeating\\ninitialization confirms the same identity; it cannot silently replace a store.\\nThe readable name `hosted-artifact-poc` is a display name, outside revision hashes.\\nClients obtain the UUID from initialization output or authenticated status.\\nRequests never allocate projects and never take a principal identity on trust.\\n\\nThe reference source is `https://github.com/mmzen/se_harness`, Git SHA-1 commit\\n`82f5a0ed7438a73da8f03aee23ad02a9b8cc09e1`. The source manifest lists every formal\\nartifact path, ID, blob OID, byte length and raw SHA-256. Generate it from Git\\nblobs using the released discovery list, not Explorer output or a worktree read.\\nOn Windows, `git archive` needs `-c core.autocrlf=false`: archive defaults can\\nconvert LF to CRLF even when the blob is LF. Compare each exported artifact with\\n`git cat-file` bytes. Preserve original bytes, including CRLF when present in Git.\\n\\nThe operator mounts the pinned source/evidence snapshot read-only. Import requests\\nidentify this configured source; they cannot make the server fetch URLs or read\\narbitrary host paths. Check every manifest entry against its mounted bytes, then\\nuse the released parser for the canonical artifact set. Missing, duplicate,\\nextra or conflicting entries prevent complete import. Supporting code/evidence\\nbelongs to the immutable historical resolver, outside the 64 MiB artifact limit.\\n\\n## Revision and baseline bytes\\n\\n`server/contracts/remote-v1.json` names the exact fields. A StoredRevision contains\\n`revision_id`, `envelope` and `document_base64`. The envelope binds the full raw\\ndocument SHA-256; the store verifies it against decoded bytes. Imported provenance\\ncontains the original repository/object format/commit and Git blob OID. Draft\\nprovenance records the authenticated principal, operation key and server-assigned\\ncreation time once. An accepted retry returns the retained bytes and time.\\n\\nCanonical JSON uses UTF-8 without BOM, sorted object keys, compact separators,\\nliteral Unicode, no Unicode normalization and no floats. Reject duplicate object\\nkeys and non-finite numbers before decoding into a map. Semantic sets are sorted\\nand deduplicated before encoding: relation targets, artifact selection keys and\\nresolved relation triples. Preserve meaningful sequence order. Raw document\\nbytes receive no line-ending or Unicode conversion for the new revision scheme.\\n\\nThe revision hash input is `se-harness-artifact-revision/v1`, LF, then canonical\\nenvelope bytes. `revision_id` is `sha256:` plus the lowercase hex digest. The\\nbaseline hash input uses `se-harness-artifact-baseline/v1`, LF and the canonical\\nmanifest; its identifier is that scheme plus `:sha256:` and the hex digest.\\nNeither hash payload includes its own derived ID or a future verification record.\\nThe baseline manifest binds sorted selection, resolved revision-to-revision\\ntriples, provenance and the exact evaluator identity. A missing relation target\\nprevents a complete baseline. Saved incomplete drafts remain distinct from\\ncomplete frozen selections and from approved definitions.\\n\\nThe fixture file `canonical-v1.json` supplies exact JSON strings and hash-input\\nbytes for three connected draft artifacts, LF/CRLF, composed/decomposed Unicode,\\na body edit, sequence order and a baseline. These are synthetic byte examples,\\nnot claimed receipts. Its all-zero parent baseline is an explicit fixture marker.\\nFuture serializer tests must consume these fixed expectations; do not regenerate\\nexpected hashes from serializer output.\\n\\n## Command-specific fields\\n\\nEvery mutation carries the project ID, operation key, expected project version,\\nexact evaluator archive/payload identity, and candidate client version/wheel hash.\\nThe server checks compatibility against the qualified tuple before mutation.\\nThe authenticated principal comes from credentials; claimed component identity\\ndoes not grant authority. Reject unknown fields and contradictory selectors.\\n\\n| Operation | Required selection and content | Accepted effect |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `import` | Complete configured source manifest; no baseline/context selector | Original immutable revisions and imported baseline, deterministic report, receipt, one project-version increment |\\n| `draft-open` | Base baseline ID and selected work-order ID | New UUID context at version 0; unchanged base; receipt and project-version increment |\\n| `create-artifact` | Context ID/version, domain, supported type; ID or explicit null for allocation | New draft revision and proposed selection; context and project versions increment once |\\n| `revise-artifact` | Context ID/version, artifact ID, expected selected revision, complete base64 document | New draft revision and derived relations; replace only that context selection; increment both versions |\\n| `freeze` | Context ID/version | New immutable baseline from the resolved complete view; project version increments; context stays open with its original base and version |\\n\\nAn empty project has no baseline to select. Import therefore has no view selector.\\nOperation lookup is `GET /v1/projects/{project}/operations/{key}` and is scoped to\\nthe authenticated principal. It requires neither a baseline nor a current version.\\nReadiness also has no view selector. These are the applicable-field interpretations\\nof HAG-API-001/002, not changes to the named protocol schemes.\\n\\nThe draft view is its base plus explicit proposals. New IDs are reserved across\\nall retained project artifacts, not just the selected baseline. The command adapter\\nuses the released authoring template and allocation behavior in a disposable\\nprojection. The isolated public 0.22.1 evaluator supplies standalone draft\\nadmission. Protected lifecycle/provenance/evidence fields remain protected.\\n\\nFreeze does not rebase, close, clear or otherwise change its context. Editing that\\ncontext later creates another proposed revision. Opening a fresh context from\\nthe frozen baseline explicitly selects a new base. Repeating an already accepted\\noperation key returns its original receipt even if live versions have advanced.\\nA different request under the same principal/project/key returns conflict.\\n\\n## Atomic acceptance and reads\\n\\nBind evaluation to project version N and the exact context/revision selection.\\nIn a short explicit database transaction, conditionally change the same Project\\nguard from N to N+1 and recheck context/revision guards. Commit the new content,\\nderived edges, selection changes and accepted receipt in that transaction. A\\ncompeting guard update or constraint conflict refuses; a process mutex is not\\nthe transaction boundary. A new operation key\\nstill has its own guarded command/receipt; retrying the original key has no new\\neffect. Its archive and payload\\nare fixed by SPEC-HAG-003. Earlier Phase 1 reports retain their original 0.22.0\\nobservations and unresolved-dependency status as historical evidence.\\n\\n## Read request and response details\\n\\n`server/contracts/read-v1.json` defines the seven POST request variants and their\\nresponse shapes. HTTP path operation/project and body values must agree. MCP\\nuses the same normalized request and authenticated handler. A context selector\\nrequires its exact version. If that version has changed, refuse with 409; no\\nimplicit latest view or historical context reconstruction is promised. Freeze a\\nselection when later reads need an immutable identity. A compare request names\\ntwo views in the same project.\\n\\n| Read | Selection and returned data |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `revision` | Artifact ID and revision ID must match the selected view. Return the complete StoredRevision, including raw bytes; a known revision outside that view is an unknown selected identity |\\n| `work-context` | Selected work order, governing bindings, exact declared paths, dependencies and relevant decisions in separate fields; embed the unchanged checkpoint-free evaluator result |\\n| `compare` | Added/removed/changed artifact bindings plus added/removed resolved relation triples; a missing side of a binding is null |\\n| `impact` | The root and reverse reachability through known declared relations at the selected view, within depth; exclude the root from the returned artifact list |\\n| `lineage` | The root and connected declared verification/evidence relations, with endpoint revisions; this reports recorded links and claims, not new assurance |\\n| `check` | Only a WO, VREC, RLS or DEC accepted by the selected released checkpoint-free `check`; return its JSON unchanged with the selected binding |\\n| `cypher` | Columns and rows from the admitted query, bound to the selected view; column names and row widths agree and graph values expose only the documented public properties |\\n\\nSort domain bindings by artifact ID, paths lexically, and edges by\\n`(source.artifact_id, kind, target.artifact_id)`. Preserve evaluator output and\\nCypher row order. A read's `provenance` names the unique Git sources of its selected\\ninputs; synthetic draft-only examples may have none. Draft provenance is retained\\nin each revision envelope. Resolve every returned revision through the view.\\nFor comparison, resolve each side independently. These equality and resolution\\nchecks require the service; JSON Schema checks only their shapes.\\n\\n`complete=true` means that this response contains the whole requested answer at\\nthe stated view and no unresolved references. It can still contain draft hints,\\nopen decisions, failed gates or a missing historical binding in the unchanged\\nevaluator result. When missing bindings prevent the requested assessment, report\\n`complete=false` with `binding_unavailable` and identify the exact missing input\\nin evaluator output. Do not convert `not_assessable` into a pass.\\n\\nBudgets apply to the aggregate graph rows across all returned collections, not\\n500 rows per nested array. Paths and unresolved-reference entries also consume\\nthat allowance. The byte budget includes the entire serialized response and\\nembedded evaluator output; never truncate that JSON. Traversal stops must be\\nvisible even if the last returned node has no displayed outgoing edge. A bounded\\npartial response uses `complete=false`, the specific limit and concrete\\ninstructions to repeat at the same view with a narrower selection. That strategy\\ndoes not turn a partial work context into a governing claim. If the operation\\nhas no meaningful narrower selection, repeat with a larger budget within the\\nfixed limits; if the minimum honest response cannot fit, refuse with 429.\\nUnresolved graph targets require a new complete view, not silent continuation at\\nan altered context version. No pagination cursor or server-side read session is\\nintroduced in this initial contract.\\n\\nThe baseline GET retrieves one canonical manifest resource, not a row query:\\n`{schema: \\\"se-harness-artifact-baseline/v1\\\", baseline_id, manifest}`. Validate the\\nmanifest with `BaselineManifest`, recompute its identity, and return the full\\nselection and resolved relations. The 2 MiB response limit still applies; reject\\nan import/freeze whose complete baseline response cannot fit before committing.\\nDo not clip the manifest to the graph-query row budget or label a fragment as B.\\nOperation GET returns exactly the stored accepted `remote-result/v1` object for\\nthe authenticated principal/project/key. Status GET reports project UUID, schema\\nrevision, readiness, actual evaluator and component identities, and the supported\\nprotocols. Missing built/qualified identities keep readiness false. Neither GET\\nrequires a context selector; operation lookup never guesses an acceptance.\\n\\n## Accepted receipts, refusals and retry order\\n\\n`server/contracts/result-v1.json` defines immutable accepted receipts and stable\\nremote refusal codes. Every successful mutation returns HTTP 200 and one UUIDv4\\n`receipt_id`. Store that entire result with the operation. Bind `request_digest`\\nto SHA-256 of `se-harness-remote-command/v1`, one LF, and canonical JSON of the\\ncomplete validated command. Canonicalize manifest entries as their declared set\\nbefore hashing; retain original document bytes and all expected versions. Reject\\nduplicate manifest entries before normalization. Credentials, connection metadata\\nand transport timestamps are outside the command and digest.\\n\\nAn accepted result's project `after` equals `before + 1`. For context open,\\ncontext `before` is null and `after` is zero. Create/revise increments the context\\nonce; freeze reports equal context versions. Import has a null context version\\nrecord. The returned view names the imported/frozen baseline or resulting context;\\naffected revision IDs are sorted unique IDs created by this operation, so an\\nidentical-source reimport may report none. Receipt IDs are correlation identities,\\nnot substitutes for revision or baseline hashes.\\n`affected_artifacts` supplies the corresponding artifact/revision bindings, so\\ncreation with automatic ID allocation returns the allocated artifact ID directly.\\nIts revision set must equal `affected_revision_ids`; a refusal returns both empty.\\n\\nApply checks in this order:\\n\\n1. Authenticate and enforce project/operation access, then perform bounded strict\\n   decoding and shape checks. Reject unknown fields such as caller-supplied actor.\\n2. For a valid command, compute its request digest and inspect the accepted key.\\n   Equal digest returns the original result immediately, even after versions or\\n   the configured tuple change. Different digest returns key-reuse conflict.\\n   Current project access remains required; never evaluate a retry as a new write.\\n3. For a new key, check the supported tuple, known selections, then project,\\n   context and selected-revision guards in that order. Refuse the first mismatch.\\n4. Check source/protected input and invoke the released evaluator against the\\n   bound selection. Invalid draft/import, incomplete freeze and unavailable\\n   mandatory bindings have distinct 422 codes. Resource refusal is 429.\\n5. Recheck guards and selection in the write transaction, write all effects and\\n   receipt, then commit. On a concurrent equal-key conflict, read the winner's\\n   committed receipt. Never update a stale request's expectations automatically.\\n\\nMalformed input uses 400, unauthenticated 401, forbidden 403, unknown accessible\\nidentity 404, stale/key/source/tuple conflict 409, invalid content 422 and resource\\nrefusal 429. The schema enumerates the `HAG_REMOTE_*` codes. These codes wrap the\\nremote operation; existing evaluator codes and JSON remain unchanged. Refusals\\nhave no receipt and no affected revisions. Populate correlation/view/versions\\nonly when known and authorized; otherwise use null. When versions are returned\\non refusal, before equals after. Read refusals use null command correlation and\\nversions. Denial must not leak another project's identities or findings.\\n\\nThe schemas describe the selected evaluator profile as well as wire shapes.\\nTheir pinned evaluator constants are compatibility checks: a well-formed but\\ndifferent version/archive/payload is 409, not malformed JSON. Keep those checks\\nseparate from primitive shape decoding and accepted-key recovery. Strictly\\ndecode base64 and require its canonical encoding before digest calculation;\\ninvalid base64 is malformed input, while invalid decoded TOML is invalid draft\\ncontent. A successful shape check alone never supplies an admission decision.\\n\\nA lost response, evaluator process crash or ambiguous database commit is not an\\naccepted or refused receipt. The client reports transport uncertainty and uses\\noperation lookup or an identical retry. A 404 lookup alone cannot prove that a\\nconcurrent transaction rolled back. A known precommit failure leaves no effects;\\nan unknown commit must be reconciled against the authoritative operation store.\\n\\n## Scenario and schema qualification\\n\\n`tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json` maps all twelve\\nVER-HAG-001 cases to explicit positive/failure outcomes and storage support. Every\\nhosted execution entry is `unperformed`. Its wire examples contain synthetic\\nidentities and demonstrate shape only; their apparent receipt values are not\\nobserved acceptances. The original fixed canonical vectors remain unchanged.\\n\\nFor independent shape qualification, install `jsonschema==4.26.0` in a disposable\\nenvironment and run its Python against:\\n\\n```text\\npython -I -B tests/hosted_artifact_graph/validate_wire_contracts.py\\npython -m unittest tests.test_hosted_artifact_graph\\n```\\n\\nThe first command registers the three local schemas without network resolution,\\nvalidates fixed vectors and the complete source manifest, and exercises accepted\\nand rejected shapes. It does not introduce a core runtime dependency. The second\\ncommand checks fixed bytes and digests through the existing test entry point.\\nNeither command executes service admission, transactions, Cypher or recovery.\\n\\n## Physical representation\\n\\nProject stores identity, schema revision and the integer command guard. Artifact\\nstores project-scoped identity. Revision stores its canonical `envelope_json`,\\n`document_base64`, artifact ID, raw document digest and derived type/status.\\nBaseline stores `manifest_json`; its SELECTS edges are derived from that manifest.\\nDraftContext stores base baseline, selected work order, version and proposals.\\nOperation stores project/principal/key, semantic request digest and immutable\\n`result_json`. JSON text properties retain exact machine structures without\\nexpanding scalar fields into graph nodes.\\n\\nHAS_REVISION links Artifact to Revision. SELECTS links Baseline to Revision.\\nBASED_ON links DraftContext to Baseline. PROPOSES links DraftContext to Revision\\nwith the selected artifact ID. DECLARES links Revision to the target Artifact,\\nwith `kind` and `target_artifact_id`; resolve the target revision through the view.\\nCross-project edges, duplicate selections, and edges inconsistent with canonical\\ncontent fail import/export checks. Unresolved authoring placeholders remain\\nexplicit findings and cannot become invented valid target nodes.\\n\\nThe public Cypher surface uses the selected project's Artifact and Revision\\nnodes, its selected Baseline (or context/base), and the corresponding storage\\nedges above. Project exposes only project ID, schema revision and the observed\\ncommand version. Artifact exposes project/artifact IDs. Revision exposes its IDs,\\ntype, status, document digest, envelope JSON and document base64. Baseline exposes\\nits IDs and manifest JSON. DraftContext exposes its IDs, selected work order,\\nbase baseline and context version. DECLARES exposes kind and target artifact ID;\\nPROPOSES exposes the selected artifact ID. Other edge properties are not public.\\n\\nOperation nodes and their result JSON are private to command handling and the\\nprincipal-scoped operation lookup. They are not available through Cypher. A\\nquery cannot use internal labels/properties, an unselected revision, another\\nbaseline/context, or caller-authored project filters to widen this surface. The\\nservice must apply that projection before query execution and use the same\\nread-only transaction snapshot for selection and results. This is application\\nadmission; it does not resolve RISK-HAG-001 or prove database privileges.\\n\\n`graph-v1.cypher` supplies six composite/single uniqueness keys, key/content\\nexistence constraints and explicit lookup indexes. Memgraph requires separate\\nindexes for uniqueness constraints ([official constraint documentation](https://memgraph.com/docs/fundamentals/constraints)).\\nSchema creation must be an explicit operator step on an empty store; later\\nstartup verifies it and refuses mismatch. Explicit initialization, stored revision\\nmismatch and missing-index refusal have now been tested for the exact candidate\\nin the [qualification report](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/phase2-20261005/protocol04-assessment.md).\\n\\n## Deferred boundary and historical qualification\\n\\nCypher remains part of the sandbox: parse a narrow read grammar, constrain the\\nselected view, apply row/byte/depth/time limits and roll back the read transaction.\\nDatabase-enforced read-only access remains RISK-HAG-001; no authoritative-pilot or\\npublic-service claim is made. The current contract does not authorize a parser\\nbypass, a replacement lifecycle policy or suppression of malformed input.\\n\\nThe candidate now includes its dependency lock, image/Compose files, admission\\nadapter, transaction implementation, remote client and plugin guidance.
